paper.title: PRIME: Training Free Proactive Reasoning via Iterative Memory Evolution for User-Centric Agent
paper.central_claim: PRIME, a gradient-free framework, improves frozen LLM agents on user-centric multi-turn tasks by distilling interaction trajectories into structured experiences in three semantic zones (golden/warning/preference), evolving the library with mutation, generalization, crossover and pruning, and retrieving experiences at inference; it achieves competitive performance with RL-trained (GRPO) agents on eight UserRL environments at 5-6x fewer GPU-hours, and libraries transfer across model sizes.
paper.claim_scope: Eight UserRL environments, Qwen3-4B/8B/14B frozen agents, GPT-4o as distiller/evolver, Qwen3-32B user simulator, 100 exploration episodes per environment.

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref unavailable to the worker subagent at write time; model_type recorded per controller dispatch instruction (agent_model=haiku slot -> claude-sonnet-5-5[1m]).

signatures.object: External experience library M of structured entries (situation, action, outcome, lesson, stage, applicability conditions, zone); frozen LLM policy unchanged.
signatures.information: Full multi-turn trajectories with turn rewards and final trajectory reward R(tau) from the UserRL environments; credit assignment (reward-to-go or equalized) picks top-3 key turns; GPT-4o distills.
signatures.operation: Exploration (100 episodes/env, temperature 1.0, horizon 16) -> LLM distillation of key turns into an entry -> zone by reward threshold (golden >=0.7, warning <=0.3, else preference) -> 5 evolution cycles of probabilistic mutation (0.10), generalization (0.05), crossover (0.02) and scheduled pruning (usage <2 or success <0.3).
signatures.output: Evolved library; at inference up to 20 prefiltered candidates are shown as tools to a selection LLM which returns about 3 experiences per turn, injected zone-organized into the prompt.
signatures.conditions: Stage filter (exploration/verification/completion by turn position 25%/75%), environment compatibility, cosine similarity >=0.6.
signatures.feedback: Environment reward only (turn-level and trajectory-level); no execution tests of the edited entries.
signatures.selection_rule: Zone by reward threshold at admission; pruning by usage/success thresholds; for mutation/crossover/generalization no acceptance criterion is stated (E26, E08).
signatures.selection_data: Exploration trajectories; whether evolution uses held-aside validation episodes is not stated.
signatures.persistence: Library persists per environment and is read by later episodes; transferable across model sizes (8B library used by 4B).
signatures.later_use: Retrieved into the agent prompt at every turn of later episodes.
signatures.claimed_effect: Relative score gains over raw base across all eight environments (e.g. +193% FunctionGym for 8B), competitive with GRPO at 5-6x fewer GPU-hours.
signatures.failure_boundary: GRPO is higher on all eight environments at both 4B and 8B; transferred 8B library gives smaller gains on 4B; evolution operators are never ablated.

gap.author_gap: RL-trained user-centric agents need multi-GPU training, are opaque and non-transferable, and need retraining for new scenarios; existing approaches struggle with turn-level credit assignment.
gap.checked_gap: The cost/opacity limitation of RL for this benchmark is a real stated cost, but the paper does not establish that existing experience-memory methods (Reflexion-style lessons, MemGPT, memory agents) fail on these environments: Reflexion/ReAct are named as baselines yet no results are shown, and only two memory systems are discussed in related work. The residual claimed (turn-level credit assignment for memory construction in user-centric dialogs) is not isolated experimentally.
gap.lineage: Reflexion / verbal reflection memories -> structured experience libraries with success/failure/preference zones -> evolutionary operators on the library. RL line: UserRL GRPO with multi-turn credit assignment (the performance comparison point).
closest_adjacent: MemoryAgent RL-trained memory read/write policy (related work)
gap.residue: Per-turn credit for which dialogue moves mattered, and persistent, auditable cross-model transfer of experience - both asserted rather than isolated.
gap.stakes: Avoiding >100 GPU-hours of 8xA100 RL per environment while retaining part of the gains.
gap.method_response: Credit-assigned distillation + zones + evolution operators + stage-aware LLM retrieval.
gap.remaining_gap: No ablation of credit assignment, zones, evolution operators or retrieval; no non-evolved memory or Reflexion comparison; GRPO still far ahead on most environments; GPT-4o teacher confound.
unresolved: Whether evolution beats plain distillation memory.
Whether the gain comes from GPT-4o knowledge injected via the library rather than from the learning loop.
Whether evaluation episodes are disjoint from exploration episodes.

matches.reason: Closest original operation is adapting a frozen model by injecting retrieved reference instances instead of retraining. It differs from C03 in that PRIME writes and evolves the reference substrate from the agent own trajectories (the harness-RSI part), which the RS card does not cover; fit is partial.

rs_pattern.reason: Matched on the inference-time operation (retrieval-based conditioning of a frozen model); the library-evolution loop is covered by the domain layer.
rs_pattern.resolves_problem: no - cheaper conditioning alternatives and a held-out regime were not tested, so the conditioning-instead-of-retraining claim is only partially closed.

matches.reason: Outcome-grounded lessons (situation-action-lesson with trigger conditions) are distilled from the agents own trajectories and injected into later tasks.

Mutation, generalization, crossover and pruning are explicit edit operations on a living store; consolidation and forgetting thresholds are specified, but the effect of the edit operations is untested.

unassigned: Zone-organized (golden/warning/preference) retrieval with stage tags is a store-structure choice closest to H04 but is not an index/graph restructuring.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: RS: express tasks as conditioning (retrieved state-outcome-action instances) so a frozen model solves them without updates. Domain: write outcome-grounded lessons into an external store and inject them into later episodes. The shared operation is retrieval-time conditioning with the store as the learned state.
pattern_mapping.necessary_conditions_and_differences: RS C03 expects a unified format plus an upstream phase teaching the model to parse it and structural hold-out; PRIME has no upstream tuning and no hold-out. Domain H00/H01 expect outcome-grounded writes with a gate and maintenance; PRIME has reward-threshold admission and probabilistic edit operators but no measured admission gate.

expectations.question: Is there a contamination/data-overlap analysis between the substrate-building tasks and the evaluation tasks?
expectations.reason: Evaluation episode count and split are never stated; only 100 exploration episodes per environment are given, so overlap cannot be ruled out.

expectations.applies_when: A conditioning/retrieval method is claimed to be valuable.
expectations.question: Is the obvious cheaper alternative compared (nearest-neighbor raw trajectories, plain distillation without evolution, Reflexion)?
expectations.reason: Reflexion and ReAct are listed as baselines but no results are reported; there is no no-evolution or raw-trajectory memory arm.

expectations.applies_when: Gain is attributed to the conditioning signal.
expectations.question: Does an ablation isolate the conditioning signal from other components?
expectations.reason: Raw vs PRIME shows memory-on vs memory-off; no ablation of zones, stage tags, credit assignment, evolution or the GPT-4o distiller.

expectations.applies_when: A retrieval database is the conditioning source.
expectations.question: Is sensitivity to source quality/coverage and source-test gap characterized?
expectations.reason: Only one cross-model transfer (8B library to 4B model, same environments); no library-size, noise or domain-shift sensitivity.

expectations.question: Does a grounding signal (execution/verifier/reward) decide what becomes a lesson?
expectations.reason: Trajectory reward thresholds and turn-level credit decide zone and key turns.

expectations.applies_when: Lessons come from success and failure trajectories.
expectations.question: Is guidance built by contrasting successes and failures rather than narrating one trajectory?
expectations.reason: Success and failure experiences are stored in separate zones, but distillation operates on single trajectories; no paired contrast of success vs failure on the same task.

expectations.question: Is there explicit maintenance (localized edits, consolidation, forgetting)?
expectations.reason: Mutation/generalization/crossover/pruning with probabilities and pruning thresholds exist, but no evidence they help or that edited entries are validated.

expectations.question: Is there a gate (execution test, quality filter, versioned merge) on what is kept?
expectations.reason: Admission is by reward-threshold zone; mutations are applied without a stated acceptance test; no versioning or rollback.

expectations.applies_when: The paper applies the attempt-reflect-store-retrieve loop to a particular vertical.
expectations.question: Is the novelty more than applying the generic loop to another vertical (user-centric multi-turn)?
expectations.reason: Turn-level credit assignment, stage tags and evolution operators go beyond the generic loop, but none is isolated experimentally, so the domain remains the main differentiator.

source_refs: Paper own claim that evolution operators refine the library (Sec.3.2)
expectations.applies_when: A multi-operator evolution procedure is claimed to improve the store.
expectations.question: Is the evolved library compared with a distillation-only (no evolution) library on the same budget?
expectations.reason: No such arm; the five evolution cycles are never shown to change scores.

expectations.applies_when: A stronger external model writes the memory consumed by a smaller frozen agent.
expectations.question: Is the teacher confound controlled (e.g. static GPT-4o-written hints, or same-model distillation)?
expectations.reason: Library content is authored by GPT-4o; no same-model or static-hint control.

expectations.question: Do the reported scores support competitiveness with GRPO on the environments?
expectations.reason: GRPO exceeds PRIME at both sizes on every one of the eight environments; near parity only on IntentionGym and SearchGym (within about 2-4%), far behind on TravelGym, FunctionGym and TauGym.

claims.text: PRIME improves frozen Qwen3 agents over raw baselines on eight UserRL environments.
claims.setting: Qwen3-4B/8B/14B frozen, library built per environment from 100 exploration episodes with GPT-4o distillation and 5 evolution cycles.
claims.selection_vs_test: Not stated; evaluation episodes vs exploration episodes unspecified.
claims.result_denominator: Single score per environment/model, no variance, no evaluation-episode count; relative gains from +0.5% to +218%.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Under the unstated evaluation protocol, adding the library raised mean task-completion scores in all 24 model-environment cells (single run); the cause cannot be attributed to the learning loop vs the GPT-4o-authored content.

claims.text: PRIME is competitive with GRPO-trained agents at 5-6x fewer GPU-hours.
claims.result_denominator: GRPO above PRIME on 8/8 environments at both sizes.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Competitive only on near-ceiling environments; GPU-hour saving excludes GPT-4o API and inference-time selection calls.

claims.text: Experience libraries transfer across model architectures.
claims.setting: 8B-built library applied to Qwen3-4B on four environments.
claims.result_denominator: Figure 4(b) only; gains smaller than native.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Within the same model family and environments a library gives modest gains; no cross-family or cross-task transfer shown.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: A reward-thresholded, GPT-4o-distilled experience library injected into prompts raised scores of frozen Qwen3 agents over their raw versions on UserRL environments in the authors single-run results; competitiveness with GRPO holds only on near-ceiling environments.
not_supported: That evolution operators, credit assignment or zones contribute (never ablated).
Retained improvement on held-out tasks (split not stated, so selection/test separation cannot be verified).
Cost advantage once GPT-4o and selection LLM calls are counted.
assessment.reproduction_note: Author-reported; not reproduced; evidence_level capped at task because selection and evaluation episodes cannot be shown to be disjoint.

G.reason: A cost/opacity limitation of RL is stated, but the specific residual against existing experience-memory agents is not established: Reflexion/ReAct are named baselines without results, and related work covers only MemGPT and MemoryAgent. The domain (user-centric multi-turn) plus gradient-free framing is the main differentiator, i.e. the F1/F2 failure shapes of the domain card.

M.reason: The mechanism (reward-gated zones, key-turn credit, stage-aware retrieval) is coherent and partly argued with examples, but the rationale for evolution operators is analogical (forward gradient), the credit method is hand-picked per environment, and no distinguishing prediction against plain reflective memory is offered.

X.reason: Hyperparameters for zones, retrieval and evolution are listed and the retrieval pipeline is described, but there is no acceptance test or version/rollback for edited entries, no conflict/staleness handling beyond usage/success pruning, and the order/selection of operator application is probabilistic with no stated validation data.

E.measurement.reason: Environment task-completion scores from the adopted UserRL benchmark are objective-ish, but they are produced with an LLM user simulator whose variance is unquantified, the number of evaluation episodes is unstated, GRPO rows may come from a different run setup, and one relative gain (SearchGym 14B +35%) is mis-printed (+74%).

E.causality.reason: Only raw vs PRIME (store-off) is available. No ablation of zones, credit assignment, evolution operators, or retrieval; no Reflexion/ReAct results; GPT-4o authoring of the library is an uncontrolled confound; cost comparison omits API calls.

E.holdout.reason: No statement of how evaluation episodes relate to the 100 exploration episodes per environment; no held-out environment or task family; the only transfer test is the 8B library applied to the 4B model on the same environments.
search_scope: Full text Sec.4.1-4.2 and Appendices A-D searched for evaluation episode count, train/test split, held-out environments, seeds, contamination analysis: none found

E.statistics.reason: All Table 1 entries are single numbers with no standard deviation, seeds, intervals or episode counts, although a stochastic user simulator and temperature-1.0 rollouts are used.
search_scope: Table 1 and surrounding text; Sec.4.2 and Appendix D searched for seeds, standard deviation, confidence intervals, significance tests, run counts: none found

E.cost.reason: GPU-hour comparison to GRPO is given (5-6x fewer; over 100 GPU-hours of 8xA100 for RL), but the statement that only forward passes through the frozen base model are needed conflicts with GPT-4o distillation/evolution and an inference-time selection LLM; API cost and search/evolution call counts are not reported.

reason: Full text with appendices read; two E items are not_reported after complete search; no missing material.
